html:
The Contras were rebel armies that fought the Sandinista government of Nicaragua from 1981 to 1990, armed and paid by the United States. Some 30,000 people died in the war.

The first Contras were former National Guardsmen of the Somoza era, based in Honduras. Peasants angry at Sandinista rule and Miskito fighters on the Caribbean coast later joined. The rebels attacked farms, cooperatives and schools as well as soldiers. The United States mined Nicaragua's harbours in 1984, which the World Court later ruled illegal.

When Congress banned aid, officials of the Reagan administration secretly sold arms to Iran to fund the Contras, the Iran-Contra affair. The war and an American trade embargo ruined the economy of Nicaragua. The peace plan of Óscar Arias led to elections in 1990, won by Violeta Chamorro.
sum: The Contras were rebel armies that fought the Sandinista government of Nicaragua from 1981 to 1990, armed and paid by the United States. Some 30,000 people died in the war.
